correctness.rationale: The proof gives a bijection from nonnegative (u,v) coefficient pairs to modular seeds, derives their first two weights case-by-case and proves the unique global maximum T. Algebraic identities (b+1)G=H+bA and b(b+1)=A-1 were checked. Exact standalone verification independently enumerated all second thresholds for b=2..60 (75,697 residue classes) and performed full denumerant DP for b=2..32; these are supplements, not the proof of infinitely many b. Residues r=0, 1..b² (including e=0), and b²<r<A and all endpoint inequalities are explicit.

evidence: Branco, Colaço, Ojeda arXiv:2112.01106, Theorems 6, 15, 22 and Section 6 treat the exact generalized repunit generators but compute ordinary Apéry/Frobenius/genus/type, not p=1.

The present triple has third entry 2a-1; its shape cannot arise for v>=1 and k>=3 because the third entry in that source is at least a+2d, and for k>=4 at least 2a+3d, whereas 2a-1 cannot equal the k=3 case unless a=2d+1 (here a=b²+b+1 and d=b, impossible b>=2).

broader_coverage.reasoning: The object-specific ordinary Frobenius theorem does not count multiple solutions and hence does not imply this formula by mere parameter substitution. The strongest checked p-Frobenius triple result applies to a different generator relation: for k=3, v=1 gives the third generator a+2d; v>=2 gives at least 2a+3d. k>=4 gives at least 2a+3d. With a=b²+b+1 and d=b, the equality a+2d=2a-1 would require b=1. No inspected theorem explicitly or via stronger stated parameter coverage evaluates this second Apéry maximum.

value.rationale: An explicit sharp parameter-uniform one-Frobenius invariant and a unique extremizing residue are substantial extra structure beyond the ordinary Frobenius number: they determine exactly how far single-factorization integers persist in a published infinite three-generator family. The parameter b spans all integers >=2 and was motivated by the generalized repunit and p-Frobenius literature, not an arbitrary finite slice.
